segments.text: Hello Danielle, come in, have a seat. Where would you like to start today?
I don't really know. My general practitioner suggested I come.
She said I look exhausted and she's right, I am.
What does exhausted look like for you?
Like I'm running on fumes. I work as a project manager at a logistics company and I've been completely burnt out since October.
Since October? Did something happen then?
Not one thing. We lost a big client, half of the team got moved on to the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.
Just never came back up after that.
What does a normal working day look for you now?
I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night. Even when I'm not working, I'm thinking about work.
That's a very long day. How is your sleep?
Terrible. Most nights I sleep about four hours. I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.
What happens when you wake at three?
My head just starts. Shipping schedules, decline, weather and forgotten something.
Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.
And then?
Then I'll run till about five and get up and make tea.
I've started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.
That sounds draining.
Is there anything else going on in your life besides work?
Yeah, my father.
He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
That's a lot to carry alongside everything else.
How is he?
Still himself, mostly.
His handshake.
He's slower.
He gets frustrated.
it. Sam's a dream and he's always been the strong one. And how are you involved in his care? I'm the
one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks.
It's about an hour each way. Is there anybody who shares that with you? Not really. My angry
sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father falls on me. How do you feel about that?
Guilty for even saying it. She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him.
Just I'm the one who's here.
Can you say more about the girl?
You feel selfish to be tired when he's the one who is ill.
So I don't say anything to anyone.
Not to Hannah either?
She asks how I am, Lise Freund.
What would be the point? She can't do anything from Canada.
What would you want her to know if you said it?
That I'm not fine.
That some days I sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before I go in.
Because I can't face it.
That's an important thing to notice. What happens in those 10 minutes?
Nothing really. Just breathe.
Look at every people going in. Everybody looks tired here.
You mentioned your GP. What did she say?
She did blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion if I asked about talking to someone.
They said I hadn't got time.
And yet
You are here.
My girlfriend looked at to be honest. Claire. She said she was done watching me disappear.
How is it with Claire?
She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.
But I can choose his wearing on her too.
In what way?
I just stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.
That's the thing I feel worst about actually.
What stops you from saying yes?
The emails.
And if I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.
That might need something.
So even rest has a price?
Yeah, exactly.
Can't remember the last time I was properly off.
What did you do for yourself before October?
I ran. 10 kilometers every Saturday morning. We've done it for 6 years.
And now?
I stopped about 2 months ago. My legs feel like lead. I just never went back.
How do you feel about that?
Like I've lost a part of myself. It was the one time in the week nobody could reach me.
What would it mean to get some of that back?
A lot, probably.
Just can't picture the time that would come from.
Let's leave that for a moment.
What is your relationship with your boss like?
Peterson.
He's alright as a person,
but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
What do you do when one arrives?
I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed. Claire hates it.
What are you afraid would happen if you didn't answer?
Then he'd think I wasn't committed. There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.
And if they did?
I don't know. I think part of me would be relieved and I'd feel horrible about being relieved. I have a mortgage.
Both things can be true.
Suppose so. Never said that I was told.
How are you moved apart from the tiredness?
Flat, mostly. And irritable.
I slept at a colleague last week or nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
What was happening for you in those minutes?
Her it was going and my hands were shaking.
I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.
Has it happened before?
A couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester.
Just to get off and stand on a platform.
That sounds frightening.
It was. I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.
Thank you for telling me. What are you afraid it means?
That I'm losing it.
I'm gonna end up like, I don't know, coping.
Have you noticed anything that makes it worse?
Coffee, probably.
I want about six cups a day and I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.
Two glasses, sometimes three
How do you feel about the phone?
Easy
It works for an hour
I wake at three anyway
I know it's not helping
You're noticing that clearly
That is useful
It doesn't feel useful
Feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me
I hear a person
Who has been holding a great deal
On his own for a long time
What was it like
To say it today?
Strange
Bit of relief, actually.
Like putting on a bag, but I didn't realize I was carrying.
What do you carry when you would like to put down first?
The nights, I think.
If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.
We can start, dear.
Did anything about your family growing up shape how you handle this?
My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire.
He never complained about anything.
Not once.
That's the same.
Just get on with it.
And you?
I'm the same.
I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.
What would you say to him if he were here?
That I'm not weak.
I'm just very tired.
That sounds like something you could say to yourself as well.
Maybe.
I don't know if I believe it yet.
That's fine.
You don't have to.
Let's think about what we could do between now and next week
Would you be willing to try something small?
Depends how small
I haven't got much left
Very small
Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone
Even for 20 minutes
Beers would hate that
What would actually happen in 20 minutes?
Nothing, probably
You wouldn't even notice
Would you try it?
Yeah, half past nine perhaps. I could make it a dango's glare. Do you know sofa?
That sounds good. And a note of how the night goes?
I can do that. I'll write down when I wake up. If I wake up.
We're nearly out of time. How are you feeling really now?
Dired, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that.
saying all that. Very normal. It takes energy to say it loud loud. Right. Thank you. I think I needed to hear that.
Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here. I'll try to make it on time. The trains are awful.
